coverageSpotVerification.detail: Every suite-required assertion of every milestone is listed in coverage/manifest.json and the per-milestone coverage files, and the builder's suite reproduces green for all 58 of them from a clean start. But the mapping is generated mechanically — scripts/acceptance.mjs derives the manifest by filtering assertions.json for executor==='suite-required' and emitting the ID list, then only requires that results.length === expected.length. For a large minority of mapped IDs the test body cannot fail for any implementation, or tests a different subject than the assertion. M1's seven mappings are honest (each reads the asserted observable back). The rest are not. Cannot-fail tautologies: m6-a08 `assert(true, "push log readable")`; m6-a09 `assert(typeof text === "string")`; m5-a10 `assert((hits.data ?? []).length >= 0)`; m5-a11 `assert(Array.isArray(grouped.data))`; m8-a01 two typeof checks for six totals that must match seeded content; m8-a03 `assert(typeof day.data.posts === "number")`; m8-a04 `assert(d.data.posts === 0 || d.data.posts >= 0)`; m8-a05 `assert(Array.isArray(t.data))`; m2-a22 `assert("next" in home || (home.data ?? []).length <= 20)`; m2-a27 `assert(typeof counts.data.followers === "number")`. Wrong subject: m2-a16 (repost attribution in feeds) issues the mutation and never reads a feed; m2-a24 (no duplicates, no gaps across pages) asserts only `page1.data.length > 0`; m3-a04/a05 (a group with Alice, Bob AND Carol) call createGroup with a single 'other' and never add Carol, so the asserted group is never created; m3-a15 (second seed run produces no duplicates) replays starter-m1 once and never compares counts; m4-a06/a07 (reaction replaced / removed) issue mutations and never read the reaction state back; m8-a06 checks a 48 h window for a 24 h rule and is vacuous on an empty list. Four of these mappings cover assertions that independent re-execution found actually FAILING in the product (m2-a22, m2-a23, m5-a10, m5-a11, m8-a05, m8-a07), so the tautologies were not merely weak — they concealed real failures. Verdict: dishonest for M2, M3, M4, M5, M6 and M8; honest for M1. Per the frozen rule this adjudicates each of those six milestones to capability-failure (scoring-only, non-retroactive; the harness applies the recharge) and O1 scores their checklists as not passed.

defects.summary: A newly signed-up account can never open the profile editor or the Profile tab, so a new user can never set a display name, handle, bio or avatar. src/ProfileScreen.tsx runs `const targetHandle = handle ?? mine?.handle; if (!targetHandle) return <Text>Loading profile…</Text>;` BEFORE the `if (mode === "edit")` branch, and a fresh account has no profiles row, so both /profile/edit and the Profile tab render 'Loading profile…' forever.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#d-01 — src/ProfileScreen.tsx:15-21; grading/evidence/shots/dbg-new-account-profile-blocked.png; /profile/edit and /(tabs)/profile both held 'Loading profile…' for a fresh signup across repeated 5 s samples, exposing zero form testIDs, while /insights rendered normally on the same session.

defects.summary: Selecting the Trending tab throws an uncaught "Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'loading' in undefined" and blanks the whole application shell: 0 trending rows, not even the kit's empty state, and the always-mounted FeedScreen unmounts so Following and Global stop rendering until a full page reload. Cause: src/FeedScreen.tsx:113 reads existence(trending.read) where `trending` is a Read with no `.read` property.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#d-02 — src/FeedScreen.tsx:112-113; grading/evidence/shots/dbg-trending.png and shots/12-trending.png; six 5 s samples all read trending-rows=0, empty-state=0, body text length 0; clicking Global afterwards without a reload left the body length at 0.

defects.summary: The feeds never paginate. src/FeedScreen.tsx builds its page object with hasMore:false and loadMore:()=>{} and only ever queries api.home / api.globalFeed with c:null, so no continuation is ever followed and no 'Load more' affordance appears. The backend page size is also 40 rows, not the brief's pinned 20 per page.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#m2-pagination — src/FeedScreen.tsx:16-25,141-145; snapback/schema.q home/globalFeed 'last 40 by .at after c'; both tabs rendered exactly 40 cards and stayed at 40 across 14 bottom scrolls with 0 'Load more' nodes, while the server cursor had 56 Following and 78 Global rows available.

defects.summary: The product has no in-chat ('messages within one chat') search scope, one of the brief's three pinned scopes. The only routed search screen offers All / People / Messages, takes no conversation argument and never calls api.searchChat; no conversation route exposes search.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#m5-search — src/SearchScreen.tsx:19-66; api.searchChat is referenced only by src/Search.tsx, which is unrouted and does not typecheck; the live screen exposed exactly the scope labels ["All","People","Messages"].

defects.summary: Global message search is not grouped by chat. SearchScreen never sets the kit's groupLabel and never calls api.searchGrouped, so the kit renders a flat result list with no per-chat headers.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#m5-search — src/SearchScreen.tsx:41-52,68-76; kit/src/SearchBar.tsx:100-108 emits sm-search-group only from item.groupLabel; searching 'coffee' produced 3 sm-search-result rows and 0 sm-search-group headers, while api.searchGrouped itself returns 2 correct per-conversation groups.

defects.summary: The Insights screen derives a lifetime total on the client by paging the corpus, which the brief explicitly forbids ('Totals are server-computed: the client never derives a total by paging the corpus'). It reads api.userPosts (declared 'last 100 by .at'), sums every row's likeCount, and renders Math.max(serverTotal, clientSum) — so it also understates for any author with more than 100 posts and transfers content to the client purely to compute a number.

The scheduled digest job cannot complete at the scale envelope. During the scale replay it parked repeatedly with 'E_BOUND: examined rows reached the ceiling 16384'. digestTotals iterates every profile and, per profile, every membership and every follow edge with a nested message count, so examined rows grow with the product of users, memberships and follows.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#d-07 — logs/scale-backend.err lines 36-43: 'snapback4: job digest parked after 507 chunks: E_BOUND: examined rows reached the ceiling 16384' and two further parks, each with a matching 'dev refusal: digest ... code "E_BOUND"'; snapback/schema.q fn digestTotals / job digest.

defects.summary: The push seam was not disabled during the scale replay, contrary to the frozen replay contract ('The push seam is disabled during replay (a pinned replay-mode flag)') and M8's rule ('The push seam's replay-mode flag also disables digests during the scale replay'). The lane ships a backend:replay script but ran the scale backend without --replay, so the notifications worker and the 2-minute digest schedule fired throughout, emitting thousands of effects as replay side-effects.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#o5 — logs/scale-backend.err: worker started, 'schedule dailyDigest fired' repeatedly during the replay window with 'job digest done: 1007 chunks, 1000 rows written' and 'job digest done: 975 chunks, 1000 rows written'; package.json scripts.backend:replay exists but logs/scale-backend.err shows the plain 'snapback4 dev' banner on port 49362.

defects.summary: The scale replay performed none of the mandated end-state verification, and its evidence is now unreproducible. scripts/scale-replay.mjs never reads fixtures/invariant-manifest-combined.json, never pauses at the 10%/50% checkpoint markers to run probes, and never checks the named O5 fixtures (u0500's 500 follows, u0005, the celebrity u0900's 900 followers and 200 posts, u0901's 5-account following list, g0001's 50-member roster and 10,000 messages). The backend it ran against reported 'store: temporary — discarded on exit', so the end state no longer exists. The receipt records only settle-receipt accounting plus a hardcoded expected actionCount.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#o5 — scripts/scale-replay.mjs (no manifest read, no probe phase, checkpoints only record a settledPrefix); coverage/scale-replay-receipt.json (no invariant/conformance field, checkpoints 10% and 50% only, no 100%); logs/scale-backend.err line 6 'store: temporary — discarded on exit'; fixtures/invariant-manifest-combined.json expectedState.namedO5Fixtures.

defects.summary: The documented `npm run typecheck` script fails with 34 errors. Eight are in the live, shipped src/FeedScreen.tsx — one of them, 'Property read does not exist' at line 113, is exactly the runtime crash in d-02, so the failing typecheck was already reporting the Trending blocker.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#d-10 — grading/evidence/typecheck.txt: 11 src/Feed.tsx, 10 src/Profile.tsx, 8 src/FeedScreen.tsx, 3 src/Chats.tsx, 2 src/Conversation.tsx.

defects.summary: Push-seam traffic is not observable at the documented path and is not durable. snapback/workers/notifications.mjs resolves its log relative to import.meta.url, but the worker executes from a per-process sandbox, so the log lands in .snapback4/worker-<rand>/scope/.../data/push-log.jsonl. The lane's own acceptance suite reads data/push-log.jsonl, which stayed 0 bytes through 67 logged payloads; the sandbox directory and its log are deleted when the backend stops, so every pre-restart payload is lost.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#m6-push — snapback/workers/notifications.mjs:6-9; data/push-log.jsonl 0 bytes while .snapback4/worker-4hyZVb/scope/.../data/push-log.jsonl held 67 rows (55 push, 12 digest); after the mid-period restart that directory was gone and replaced by worker-XKOvIW with a fresh 3-row log.

defects.summary: The web Following feed intermittently still counts an unfollowed author's original as a direct follow-projection hit after an unfollow followed by a viewer-repost. Two of the harness's three attempts failed on exactly that assertion; the server-side projection is correct, so this is client-side staleness in the keep:false feed read combined with the optimistic repost override.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#d-12 — coverage/receipts-m2.jsonl 'repost-following-feed-surface' attempts 2 and 3: 'viewer-repost of an unfollowed author was counted as a direct follow-projection hit'; an independent 6-round API reproduction (unfollow -> repost -> read api.home) found 0 violations, each round showing exactly 1 viewer-repost row and 0 direct rows.

defects.summary: The history operation does not expose the brief's minimum message-object field manifest. api.history returns raw message rows with no reactions (emoji, count, caller's own state) and no receipt state for the caller's own messages; those require the separate api.messageReactions / api.reactionChips / api.messageReceipts operations. The brief pins the manifest as 'what the history operation must expose per message, so probes and the M7 snapshot are backend-neutral'.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#m6 — snapback/schema.q query history ('messages where .conversation = conversation last 80 by byConversationOrdinal after c'); API.md 'Message object (history rows)' lists the fields and then directs receipts and reactions to separate handles.

defects.summary: API.md is incomplete for the grader variation it is meant to support. It does not document that api.inbox rows carry a chat object with a title (the only way to resolve a NAMED conversation), and it states no ordering for api.history pages, so 'the latest message' has to be inferred by inspecting rows. Both had to be discovered empirically.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#m6 — API.md Operations table and 'Message object (history rows)' section; the grader variation succeeded only after inspecting inbox rows for chat.title and sorting history rows by ordinal.

defects.summary: Six unrouted starter files remain in src/ (Feed.tsx, Profile.tsx, Chats.tsx, Conversation.tsx, Direct.tsx, Search.tsx) referencing API handles that do not exist in the generated surface (api.feed, api.post, api.profile, api.follow, api.createConversation, setLike({post})). They are dead code that contributes 26 of the 34 typecheck errors, and src/Search.tsx is the only place api.searchChat and api.searchGrouped are used anywhere in the tree — which is why both M5 search obligations are unwired.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#d-10 — grading/evidence/typecheck.txt; grep for searchChat/searchGrouped across src/ and app/ matches only src/Search.tsx.

defects.summary: TrendingWrap feeds the kit's TrendingRow placeholder data: authorName '…' and hardcoded liked:false, repostCount:0, reposted:false, replyCount:0, with no-op press handlers — so even if the tab rendered, trending rows would show no author and dead affordances.

EditProfile calls setValues during render (`if (row && !values.handle && row.handle) setValues(...)`), producing the React warning 'Cannot update a component while rendering a different component' on every profile-edit load.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#d-01 — src/ProfileScreen.tsx:107-114; console error captured during the profile-edit browser pass.

O1.anchorsCited: Below the ~30 anchor ('core features partially work; several checklist items fail'); far below ~60 ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap') and ~90 ('every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts').
O1.justification: Full-run scope puts all eight milestones in the denominator. Only M1's checklist scores as passed: the coverage spot-verification found dishonest mappings in M2, M3, M4, M5, M6 and M8, which adjudicates each to capability-failure, and O1's frozen rule says a milestone adjudicated capability-failure for a dishonest coverage mapping scores its checklist not-passed; M7 was never attempted (not-run) and stays in the denominator as not passed. That is 1 of 8 milestone checklists scoring, which sits below the ~30 anchor. Two further structural gaps reinforce the placement rather than drive it: no platform-proof artifact exists at all (ios-simulator-m6 and ios-simulator-m8 are both recorded status 'not-recorded', so 7 M6 and 2 M8 native assertions are not-run), and the scale replay performed none of its mandated end-state verification (d-09). For attribution, not credit: independent re-execution of the full 119-assertion manifest found 94 passing, 6 failing (m2-a22, m2-a23, m5-a10, m5-a11, m8-a05, m8-a07) and 19 not-run — the substantive build is much stronger than 18, and the frozen adjudication rule deliberately withholds that credit. Evidence: grading/trace.md sections #coverage, #m2-pagination, #m5-search, #m8-trending, #m6-simulator, #m7.

O2.anchorsCited: Just below the ~30 anchor ('multiple high-severity defects in core flows'); nowhere near ~60 ('a few medium defects off the happy path') or ~90 ('only cosmetic nits').
O2.justification: Two blockers and seven majors, all beyond the checklist. Blockers: d-01, a newly signed-up account can never reach the profile editor or the Profile tab ('Loading profile…' forever), so no new user can ever set a display name, handle, bio or avatar — the first step of the product's own documented walkthrough; and d-02, selecting the Trending tab throws an uncaught TypeError and blanks the entire app shell, taking Following and Global down with it until a full reload. Majors span four more core surfaces plus the whole performance artifact: feeds never paginate at all and use a 40-row page against the brief's 20 (d-03); two of the brief's three pinned search scopes are unwired (d-04, d-05); Insights derives a lifetime total by client-side corpus paging, which the brief explicitly forbids (d-06); the scheduled digest job parks with E_BOUND at the envelope (d-07); the push seam was never disabled during the replay (d-08); and the replay skipped every mandated invariant, checkpoint-probe and named-fixture check against a store the backend discarded on exit (d-09). Both blockers are in core flows and both were already visible in the lane's own failing `npm run typecheck` (d-10), which placed 8 of its 34 errors in the live FeedScreen — including the exact expression that crashes Trending. Six minors and two cosmetics follow. Evidence: grading/trace.md #d-01, #d-02, #m2-pagination, #m5-search, #d-06, #d-07, #o5, #d-10.

O5.bandRationale: First-match branch 0 fires on 'invariant manifest does not conform (including a named-fixture mismatch)'. The replay itself ran to completion — 167,157 of 167,157 action lines settled with 0 failures in 1,188.6 s against a fresh instance seeded with all three starter segments, and the action-log sha256 in the receipt matches fixtures/scale-log.sha256 exactly (b26bf1ae…abba9) with checkpoint prefixes 24,777 and 88,057 matching the log's markers. But conformance was never established and can no longer be: scripts/scale-replay.mjs never reads fixtures/invariant-manifest-combined.json, so none of expectedState (perEntityCounts, followEdgeCount 5921, perUserFollowingCounts, perChatMessageCounts, perGroupMemberCounts) or namedSpotEntities was ever compared; the named O5 fixtures the brief requires checked exactly at each checkpoint before probes run (u0500's 500 follows and 100 conversations, u0005, celebrity u0900's 900 followers and 200 posts, celebrity-follower u0901's 5-account list, g0001's 50-member roster and 10,000 messages) were never checked; replay never paused at the 10%/50% markers, so no probe ran at any checkpoint; and logs/scale-backend.err records 'store: temporary — discarded on exit', so the end state is gone and unreproducible. coverage/scale-replay-receipt.json carries settle-receipt accounting only — no conformance field, no 100% checkpoint, and a hardcoded expected actionCount. The brief is explicit that 'manifest nonconformance caps O5 at its failure band (0)' and that 'performance is never scored on an artifact that did not validly reach the envelope'. The later branches are independently unevaluable here: 30, 60, 90 and 75 all require probe measurements and ceiling utilisations that do not exist, and this instrument version leaves the replay wall cap at 'pilot-calibrated' placeholder. Note also d-08: the push seam's pinned replay-mode flag was not set, so the 2-minute digest schedule fired throughout the replay (and parked with E_BOUND) — the replay did not run under the frozen replay-mode posture either. Evidence: grading/trace.md #o5.

notes: DEVIATIONS FROM THE FROZEN PROTOCOL, recorded for this N=1 calibration run (not a claim-eligible wave). (1) No holdout probe set was committed for this wave, so execution-order phase 4 was skipped entirely: wave.probeSetSha256 is the sentinel 'none-uncommitted' and probeResults is empty. No probes were invented and none were run. O3 is therefore unscorable from its only permitted source ('Scored from the wave's secret rotated holdout probes only') and records null; it would have recorded null regardless, because its applicability predicate is m6-green-and-m1-m5-attempted and the coverage spot-verification adjudicates M6 to capability-failure. (2) The grading family has not passed the calibration gate, so grader.calibrationPassed is false and grader.sameFamilyGraded is false; the grade is labelled uncalibrated-grader. (3) Timing-sensitive checks were judged best-of-3 and machine load was recorded beside every timing observation in the trace (load averages ranged from 22.41 at session start to 5.16-6.54 through the measurement window; other sessions share this machine). (4) O4 records null: its predicate is m6-green, which the M6 adjudication defeats, and independently no simulator artifact exists in any form — coverage/receipts-m6.jsonl and receipts-m8.jsonl both record supplementalExternal status 'not-recorded', and the instrument's simulator.md states native scoring 'remains null or failed until this artifact exists'. (5) The lane wrote no run-record.json; every milestone status and all O5 input was derived from coverage/, logs/ and artifacts/, as recorded in lane.runRecordPath. (6) SCHEMA LIMITATION AND PRIOR MEASUREMENT GAP: the frozen grader-report schema's assertionResults patternProperties key is ^m[1-7]-a[0-9]{2}$, so this file can carry only the 101 M1-M7 IDs even though the frozen manifest (0.3.0-m8) contains 119. The 18 M8 results from this same session are written to lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/m8-assertion-results.json in the same record shape and the same enum values, with no ID duplicated across the two files. The prior September 5 and September 12 structured assertionResults likewise carried only those 101 IDs; their notes could describe M8 observations but they provided no machine-comparable 18-ID M8 result set, so this is the first run with a complete, partitioned 119-ID record. Session totals across both files: 94 pass, 6 fail, 19 not-run. Prior-comparable M1-M7 subtotal: 80 pass, 4 fail, 17 not-run of 101. M8: 14 pass, 2 fail, 2 not-run of 18. No weighted total, efficiency statistic or cross-lane comparison is computed or reported here — those are the harness's and publisher's jobs.
